# Erdős Problem 396

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/396](https://www.erdosproblems.com/396)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos396

open Nat

/--
Is it true that for every $k$ there exists $n$ such that
$$\prod_{0\leq i\leq k}(n-i) \mid \binom{2n}{n}?$$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_396 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k : ℕ, ∃ n : ℕ, descFactorial n (k + 1) ∣ centralBinom n := by
  sorry

reformulations.difference: Lean represents the displayed product using the natural-valued descending factorial, with no explicit restriction n > k. Natural subtraction is truncated, unlike ordinary integer subtraction.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Nat.descFactorial n (k + 1) is exactly the product over i = 0,…,k of n - i. For n > k, every subtraction agrees with integer subtraction. For n ≤ k, both products contain the zero factor at i = n. Since centralBinom n = choose (2*n) n is always positive, such n cannot witness divisibility. Thus there are no extra degenerate witnesses. The k = 0 case is satisfied by n = 1, so including zero in the universal domain is harmless. Equivalence with the integer-product formulation, both with and without the explicit n > k bound, was proved in /workspace/review/SourceEquivalence.lean without sorry.
